description_full: Microsoft Corporation, a technology company, develops and supports a portfolio of technology solutions for individuals and businesses worldwide. Its products include operating systems, server applications, business solution applications, software development tools, desktop and server management tools, and video games; and devices, such as PCs, tablets, gaming and entertainment consoles, other intelligent devices, and related accessories. The company's Productivity and Business Processes segment offers Microsoft 365 Commercial, Enterprise Mobility + Security, Power BI, Exchange, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 Security and Compliance, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Windows Commercial on-premises and Office licensed on-premises. This segment also provides Microsoft 365 Consumer products and cloud services; LinkedIn, including talent solutions, marketing solutions, subscriptions, and sales solutions; Dynamics 365, a set of cloud-based applications; and on-premises ERP and CRM applications. Its Intelligent Cloud segment offers server products and cloud services; cloud and AI consumption-based services, GitHub cloud services, health and life sciences cloud services, as well as virtual desktop offerings, and other cloud services; SQL Server, Windows Server, Visual Studio, System Center, and related client access licenses; and enterprise support services, industry solutions, Microsoft partner network, and learning experience. The company's More Personal Computing segment provides Windows OEM licensing and devices comprising Surface and PC accessories; XBOX hardware, and XBOX first- and third-party content and services; XBOX Game Pass and other subscriptions; XBOX Cloud Gaming, advertising, and other cloud services; and search advertising consisting of Bing, Copilot, Microsoft News, Microsoft Edge, and third-party affiliates. It sells its products through partners and retail networks. The company was founded in 1975 and is headquartered in Redmond, Washington.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 223K people. Revenue per employee of $1.5M ranks in the top quartile among Technology peers, with revenue growing 11%/yr across its filed history. Each employee generates $300K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $56K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 9× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (5/10).
financial_summary: Microsoft Corporation is a mega-cap technology business with a $3.9T market cap on $331.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +16% over the past three years and +15% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 46% against a 10% cost of capital — a 36-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 69% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $67.0B in free cash flow — roughly 20 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.37× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 51× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.2%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 2.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sector_headwinds.text: Priced near or above estimated fair value, so the margin of safety has been bid away
Insiders are net sellers (100% sell ratio, net $31.4M) — the people closest to the business are reducing their personal stake
Technology sector lagging the market significantly, underperforming by 7% over 3 months
Elevated sector volatility (38% annualized) adds uncertainty
Antitrust and platform-regulation risk — the larger the network effect, the larger the regulatory target on its back, and a single consent decree can reset the moat.
AI disruption of existing software moats — incumbents with durable margins face commoditisation as AI-native competitors replicate features at a fraction of the R&D cost.
Cybersecurity liability and talent cost inflation — a single breach can erase years of goodwill, and the war for engineering talent compresses margins even at scale.

sector_tailwinds: Reinvestment rate supports 26% organic growth capacity — capital is compounding inside the business
Operating margins 40% above sector median — the quantitative trace of pricing power
Altman Z comfortably in the safe zone — a fortress balance sheet on this measure
22 consecutive years of dividend payments — an operating record that makes the dividend claim credible
Healthy payout ratio leaves room for both dividend growth and reinvestment
ROIC sits in the top quartile of Technology peers — the moat is wider than the neighbourhood

sect: Its 47% operating margin runs 40pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 2.00x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
It accounts for 7.5% of sector revenue and 15.0% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-2.0% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 9% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 6% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 34% and a beta of 1.11, it moves roughly with the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $10.6B traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 28% in the 2020 crash, 36% in the 2022 bear market and 56% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $476 (margin of safety -10%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 29%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $286 to $821 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: P/FCF 58.1 vs 26.1 (sector median).
The EBIT multiple is close to its own 10-year median (-7%).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 1.7% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The 54 covering analysts target $636 on average, 21% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 46% clears the cost of capital of 10.0% by 36pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.38).
It runs a 69% gross margin and converts 20% of revenue into free cash flow, or 16% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.37x.
ROE of 30% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.7x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 8pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 10.7% of revenue on R&D and 3.7% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $36.5B (1% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 9.2, in the safe zone).
It runs on negative working capital (-52 days), so customers and suppliers effectively fund its operations.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 16.1% over 3 years, 14.6% over 5 years and 14.5% over 10 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 56% of profits supports about 26.1% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 3.6% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.93 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 2.1x annual revenue and deferred revenue up 13%.
Capex runs 3.4x depreciation (34.9% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
Its Rule of 40 score is 31, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.1%), and institutions hold 76%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (12 sales, net $31.4M sold).
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.2% (0.5% in buybacks and 0.7% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 22 consecutive years, raising it 9.9% a year over the last five.
people: With about 223,000 employees, each generates about $1.5M of revenue, 4.0x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 11.0% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $300K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $13.1M (9x revenue per employee).
